subproblems.title: Continuity of a linear-form family evaluated along continuous data
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers and L := L(R^n, R^ℓ) the finite-dimensional space of (continuous) linear maps R^n → R^ℓ. Let U ⊆ R^n be open and Φ : R^n → L* = L(L, R) be such that x ↦ Φ(x)[P] is continuous on U for every P ∈ L. Let s : R^n → R^n, B : R^n → L and x₀ ∈ R^n with s(x₀) ∈ U, s continuous at x₀ and B continuous at x₀. Then x ↦ Φ(s(x))[B(x)] is continuous at x₀.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (Φ : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (s : Rn n → Rn n) (B : Rn n → Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x₀ : Rn n), IsOpen U → (∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ContinuousOn (fun x => Φ x P) U) → s x₀ ∈ U → ContinuousAt s x₀ → ContinuousAt B x₀ → ContinuousAt (fun x => Φ (s x) (B x)) x₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Lean setting: L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ is finite-dimensional over ℝ, and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ has its usual AddCommGroup/Module/NormedSpace instances at the default maxSynthPendingDepth (checked at the pin).
1. Basis and coordinates. Let b := Module.finBasis ℝ L, a basis (E_r) of L indexed by r ∈ Fin (Module.finrank ℝ L), E_r = b r. For each r let c_r : L → ℝ, c_r(P) := b.repr P r. Then c_r is the linear map b.coord r (Module.Basis.coord_apply), and every linear map on the finite-dimensional Hausdorff space L is continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional applied to b.coord r), so each c_r is continuous on L.
2. Expansion. For every P ∈ L, P = Σ_r c_r(P) • E_r (Module.Basis.sum_repr: Σ_r b.repr P r • b r = P). Since Φ(y) is linear for every y, for all x we get Φ(s(x))[B(x)] = Φ(s(x))[Σ_r c_r(B(x)) • E_r] = Σ_r c_r(B(x)) · Φ(s(x))[E_r] (rewrite B x as b.sum_repr backwards, then map_sum, map_smul, smul_eq_mul). Hence, as functions of x, (x ↦ Φ(s(x))[B(x)]) = (x ↦ Σ_r c_r(B(x)) · Φ(s(x))[E_r]) (funext), and it suffices to prove that the right-hand side is continuous at x₀.
3. Coordinate factor. For each r, x ↦ c_r(B(x)) is continuous at x₀: it is the continuous map c_r of step 1 composed with B, which is continuous at x₀ (Continuous.continuousAt composed via ContinuousAt.comp).
4. Coefficient factor. Fix r. By hypothesis (with P := E_r) the function y ↦ Φ(y)[E_r] is continuous on U. Because U is open and s(x₀) ∈ U, U is a neighbourhood of s(x₀) (IsOpen.mem_nhds), so y ↦ Φ(y)[E_r] is continuous at s(x₀) (ContinuousOn.continuousAt). Composing with s, which is continuous at x₀, shows that x ↦ Φ(s(x))[E_r] is continuous at x₀ (ContinuousAt.comp).
5. Products and the finite sum. By steps 3 and 4 and ContinuousAt.mul, every summand x ↦ c_r(B(x)) · Φ(s(x))[E_r] is continuous at x₀. A finite sum of functions continuous at x₀ is continuous at x₀ (ContinuousAt is the statement Tendsto f (𝓝 x₀) (𝓝 (f x₀)); apply tendsto_finsetSum over Finset.univ). By step 2 this sum is the function x ↦ Φ(s(x))[B(x)], which is therefore continuous at x₀. QED.
proof_key_steps: b := Module.finBasis ℝ L with continuous coordinates c_r = b.coord r (finite dimension)
Φ(s x)[B x] = Σ_r c_r(B x) · Φ(s x)[E_r] by Basis.sum_repr and linearity of Φ(s x)
c_r ∘ B continuous at x₀; y ↦ Φ(y)[E_r] continuous at s(x₀) ∈ U (U open) and composed with s
product and finite sum (tendsto_finsetSum) of functions continuous at x₀

subproblems.title: Continuity of a bilinear-form family evaluated along continuous data
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers and L := L(R^n, R^ℓ). Let U ⊆ R^n be open and a : R^n → L(L, L(L, R)) (continuous bilinear forms on L) be such that x ↦ a(x)[P][Q] is continuous on U for all P, Q ∈ L. Let s : R^n → R^n, A, B : R^n → L and x₀ ∈ R^n with s(x₀) ∈ U and s, A, B continuous at x₀. Then x ↦ a(s(x))[A(x)][B(x)] is continuous at x₀.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (a : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (s : Rn n → Rn n) (A B : Rn n → Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x₀ : Rn n), IsOpen U → (∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ContinuousOn (fun x => a x P Q) U) → s x₀ ∈ U → ContinuousAt s x₀ → ContinuousAt A x₀ → ContinuousAt B x₀ → ContinuousAt (fun x => a (s x) (A x) (B x)) x₀
subproblems.natural_proof:
Uses the sibling lemma linear_family_continuity (Lean: Submission.dohr_eb_lhr_dqwe_linear_family_continuousAt). Only the scalars a y P Q and the linear-form type L →L[ℝ] ℝ (instances available at default depth) are manipulated.
1. Basis and coordinates. Let b := Module.finBasis ℝ L, E_r := b r, and c_r(P) := b.repr P r. Each c_r = b.coord r is a linear map on the finite-dimensional space L, hence continuous (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional).
2. Expansion in the first slot. For every x, A(x) = Σ_r c_r(A(x)) • E_r (Module.Basis.sum_repr). As a(s(x)) : L → L* is linear, a(s(x))[A(x)] = Σ_r c_r(A(x)) • a(s(x))[E_r] in L* (map_sum, map_smul). Evaluating at B(x) commutes with finite sums and scalar multiples of continuous linear maps (sum_apply, smul_apply — the ContinuousLinearMap.sum_apply/smul_apply names are deprecated aliases at the pin — and smul_eq_mul), so a(s(x))[A(x)][B(x)] = Σ_r c_r(A(x)) · a(s(x))[E_r][B(x)]. By funext it suffices to show that x ↦ Σ_r c_r(A(x)) · a(s(x))[E_r][B(x)] is continuous at x₀.
3. Coordinate factor. For each r, x ↦ c_r(A(x)) is continuous at x₀ (continuous c_r composed with A, which is continuous at x₀).
4. Coefficient factor via linear_family_continuity. Fix r and define the linear-form family Φ_r(y) := a(y)[E_r] ∈ L* (Lean: fun y => a y (b r)). For every P ∈ L, y ↦ Φ_r(y)[P] = a(y)[E_r][P] is continuous on U: this is the hypothesis with first argument E_r and second argument P (Lean: fun P => ha (b r) P). Apply linear_family_continuity to Φ_r with the same open U, the same s and x₀ (s(x₀) ∈ U, s continuous at x₀) and with B (continuous at x₀): it yields that x ↦ Φ_r(s(x))[B(x)] = a(s(x))[E_r][B(x)] is continuous at x₀.
5. Products and finite sum. Each summand x ↦ c_r(A(x)) · a(s(x))[E_r][B(x)] is continuous at x₀ by steps 3, 4 and ContinuousAt.mul; the finite sum over r is continuous at x₀ (tendsto_finsetSum over Finset.univ). By step 2 this is x ↦ a(s(x))[A(x)][B(x)]. QED.
proof_key_steps: b := Module.finBasis ℝ L, coordinates c_r continuous
a(s x)[A x][B x] = Σ_r c_r(A x) · a(s x)[E_r][B x] (sum_repr in the first slot, map_sum/map_smul, sum_apply/smul_apply)
x ↦ a(s x)[E_r][B x] continuous at x₀ by linear_family_continuity applied to Φ_r(y) := a(y)[E_r]
product with c_r ∘ A and finite sum (tendsto_finsetSum)

subproblems.title: Translated weak identity: testing with a translated test function
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^ℓ), U ⊆ R^n any set, a : R^n → L(L, L(L, R)), Φ : R^n → L(L, R), v : R^n → R^ℓ arbitrary maps, and h ∈ R^n. Assume ∫_U a(x)[Dv(x)][Dζ(x)] dx = ∫_U Φ(x)[Dζ(x)] dx for every C^1 map ζ : R^n → R^ℓ with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U (Lebesgue measure; D = Fréchet derivative). Let η : R^n → R^ℓ be C^1 with compact support such that x + h ∈ U for every x ∈ tsupport η. Then ∫_{R^n} a(x + h)[Dv(x + h)][Dη(x)] dx = ∫_{R^n} Φ(x + h)[Dη(x)] dx. Here D is Mathlib's fderiv (the Fréchet derivative where it exists, 0 elsewhere) and ∫ is the Bochner integral for Lebesgue measure (0 for a non-integrable integrand); no measurability of U and no integrability or differentiability is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (a : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Φ : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (h : Rn n) (η : Rn n → Rn ℓ), (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ U → ∫ x in U, a x (fderiv ℝ v x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = ∫ x in U, Φ x (fderiv ℝ ζ x)) → ContDiff ℝ 1 η → HasCompactSupport η → (∀ x ∈ tsupport η, x + h ∈ U) → ∫ x, a (x + h) (fderiv ℝ v (x + h)) (fderiv ℝ η x) = ∫ x, Φ (x + h) (fderiv ℝ η x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Integrals are Bochner integrals with respect to Lebesgue measure (volume) on Rn n. No hypothesis on U, a, Φ or v other than the displayed weak identity is used (in particular neither measurability of U nor integrability of the integrands).
1. The translated test function. Put ζ(y) := η(y − h). Since y ↦ y − h is C^∞ (contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const) and η is C^1, ζ = η ∘ (· − h) is C^1 (ContDiff.comp). Since y ↦ y − h is a homeomorphism of R^n (Homeomorph.subRight h) and η has compact support, ζ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph).
2. Support of ζ. As y ↦ y − h is continuous, tsupport (η ∘ (· − h)) ⊆ (· − h)⁻¹(tsupport η) (tsupport_comp_subset_preimage). So if y ∈ tsupport ζ then y − h ∈ tsupport η, hence (y − h) + h ∈ U by hypothesis, i.e. y ∈ U (sub_add_cancel). Thus tsupport ζ ⊆ U.
3. Testing. By steps 1–2, ζ is admissible in the weak identity, which gives ∫_U a(y)[Dv(y)][Dζ(y)] dy = ∫_U Φ(y)[Dζ(y)] dy. By fderiv_comp_sub (valid with no differentiability hypothesis) Dζ(y) = Dη(y − h) for all y, hence ∫_U a(y)[Dv(y)][Dη(y − h)] dy = ∫_U Φ(y)[Dη(y − h)] dy.
4. Removing the restriction to U. Let y ∉ U. Then y − h ∉ tsupport η (otherwise y = (y − h) + h ∈ U). Since tsupport(Dη) ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_fderiv_subset), y − h ∉ tsupport(Dη), so Dη(y − h) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By linearity a(y)[Dv(y)][0] = 0 and Φ(y)[0] = 0 (map_zero). Hence both integrands vanish outside U, and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero converts step 3 into ∫ a(y)[Dv(y)][Dη(y − h)] dy = ∫ Φ(y)[Dη(y − h)] dy, integrals over all of R^n.
5. Translation. Lebesgue measure on Rn n is invariant under translations (an additive Haar measure on a commutative group, so IsAddRightInvariant holds), hence ∫ F(x + h) dx = ∫ F(y) dy for every F : R^n → R (integral_add_right_eq_self F h). Rewriting both sides of step 4 with F(y) := a(y)[Dv(y)][Dη(y − h)] and F(y) := Φ(y)[Dη(y − h)] gives ∫ a(x + h)[Dv(x + h)][Dη(x + h − h)] dx = ∫ Φ(x + h)[Dη(x + h − h)] dx. Since x + h − h = x (add_sub_cancel_right), this is ∫ a(x + h)[Dv(x + h)][Dη(x)] dx = ∫ Φ(x + h)[Dη(x)] dx, the claim. QED.
proof_key_steps: ζ := η(· − h) is C^1 with compact support (ContDiff.comp, HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph)
tsupport ζ ⊆ U via tsupport_comp_subset_preimage and the hypothesis
weak identity for ζ with Dζ(y) = Dη(y − h) (fderiv_comp_sub)
integrands vanish off U (tsupport_fderiv_subset, map_zero) so ∫_U = ∫_{R^n}
translate y = x + h (integral_add_right_eq_self) and simplify x + h − h = x

subproblems.title: A function continuous at every point of a compact set and vanishing off it is integrable
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, F : R^n → R and K ⊆ R^n compact. Assume F is continuous at every point of K and F(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K. Then F is Lebesgue integrable on R^n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ) (K : Set (Rn n)), IsCompact K → (∀ x ∈ K, ContinuousAt F x) → (∀ x, x ∉ K → F x = 0) → Integrable F
subproblems.natural_proof:
Integrability is with respect to Lebesgue measure (volume) on Rn n, which is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts).
1. Points of K. F is continuous at every x ∈ K by hypothesis.
2. Points off K. Let x ∉ K. K is compact in the Hausdorff space R^n, hence closed (IsCompact.isClosed), so R^n \ K is open and contains x and is therefore a neighbourhood of x (IsOpen.mem_nhds). On R^n \ K, F ≡ 0 by hypothesis, so F agrees with the constant function 0 on a neighbourhood of x (an eventual equality obtained with filter_upwards). The constant function is continuous at x, and a function eventually equal near x to a function continuous at x is continuous at x (ContinuousAt.congr). Hence F is continuous at x.
3. By steps 1–2 F is continuous at every point, hence continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt).
4. F vanishes outside the compact set K, so F has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro, R^n being an R1 space).
5. A continuous function with compact support is integrable for every measure that is finite on compact sets, in particular for Lebesgue measure on Rn n (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). QED.
proof_key_steps: continuity off K: Kᶜ open (K compact ⇒ closed), F ≡ 0 there, ContinuousAt.congr
F continuous everywhere (continuous_iff_continuousAt)
HasCompactSupport.intro from vanishing off compact K
Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport

subproblems.title: Derivative of a difference quotient
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ be natural numbers, v : R^n → R^ℓ, e, x ∈ R^n and d ∈ R (with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0, so for d = 0 both sides are 0), and assume v is differentiable at x and at x + d e. Then the derivative at x of z ↦ d⁻¹(v(z + d e) − v(z)) equals d⁻¹(Dv(x + d e) − Dv(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (v : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (e x : Rn n) (d : ℝ), DifferentiableAt ℝ v x → DifferentiableAt ℝ v (x + d • e) → fderiv ℝ (fun z => d⁻¹ • (v (z + d • e) - v z)) x = d⁻¹ • (fderiv ℝ v (x + d • e) - fderiv ℝ v x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Put g(z) := v(z + d e). The map z ↦ z + d e is differentiable with derivative the identity (differentiableAt_id.add_const), and v is differentiable at x + d e, so g is differentiable at x by the chain rule (DifferentiableAt.comp). Moreover Dg(x) = Dv(x + d e) (fderiv_comp_add_right, which holds unconditionally).
2. Since g and v are both differentiable at x, the map z ↦ g(z) − v(z) is differentiable at x (DifferentiableAt.sub) and its derivative at x is Dg(x) − Dv(x) (fderiv_fun_sub).
3. For a function differentiable at x, multiplying by the constant scalar d⁻¹ multiplies the derivative by d⁻¹: D(z ↦ d⁻¹ • (g(z) − v(z)))(x) = d⁻¹ • D(z ↦ g(z) − v(z))(x) (fderiv_fun_const_smul with the differentiability from step 2, the function written explicitly as fun z => v (z + d • e) - v z). This holds for every real d (for d = 0 both sides are 0).
4. Combining steps 1–3: D(z ↦ d⁻¹ • (v(z + d e) − v(z)))(x) = d⁻¹ • (Dv(x + d e) − Dv(x)). QED.
proof_key_steps: g(z) := v(z + d e) differentiable at x with Dg(x) = Dv(x + d e) (chain rule, fderiv_comp_add_right)
D(g − v)(x) = Dg(x) − Dv(x) (fderiv_fun_sub)
D(d⁻¹ • (g − v))(x) = d⁻¹ • D(g − v)(x) (fderiv_fun_const_smul)
